questions.q: Find the area between $y=x^2$ and $y=x+2$.
questions.answer: Intersect: $x^2=x+2 \Rightarrow x^2-x-2=0 \Rightarrow (x-2)(x+1)=0$: $x=-1,2$. On this interval $x+2 \geq x^2$. Area $=\int_{-1}^{2}\left[(x+2)-x^2\right]dx=\left[\frac{x^2}{2}+2x-\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_{-1}^{2}=\left(2+4-\frac{8}{3}\right)-\left(\frac{1}{2}-2+\frac{1}{3}\right)=\frac{10}{3}-\left(-\frac{7}{6}\right)=\frac{9}{2}$.
questions.explanation: Intersect: $x^2=x+2 \Rightarrow x^2-x-2=0 \Rightarrow (x-2)(x+1)=0$: $x=-1,2$. On this interval $x+2 \geq x^2$. Area $=\int_{-1}^{2}\left[(x+2)-x^2\right]dx=\left[\frac{x^2}{2}+2x-\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_{-1}^{2}=\left(2+4-\frac{8}{3}\right)-\left(\frac{1}{2}-2+\frac{1}{3}\right)=\frac{10}{3}-\left(-\frac{7}{6}\right)=\frac{9}{2}$.

Find the area of the region bounded by $x=y^2$ and $x=y+2$, integrating with respect to $y$.
questions.answer: Intersect: $y^2=y+2 \Rightarrow y^2-y-2=0 \Rightarrow (y-2)(y+1)=0$: $y=-1,2$. On this interval $y+2\geq y^2$. Area $=\int_{-1}^{2}\left[(y+2)-y^2\right]dy=\left[\frac{y^2}{2}+2y-\frac{y^3}{3}\right]_{-1}^{2}=\left(2+4-\frac{8}{3}\right)-\left(\frac{1}{2}-2+\frac{1}{3}\right)=\frac{9}{2}$.
questions.explanation: Intersect: $y^2=y+2 \Rightarrow y^2-y-2=0 \Rightarrow (y-2)(y+1)=0$: $y=-1,2$. On this interval $y+2\geq y^2$. Area $=\int_{-1}^{2}\left[(y+2)-y^2\right]dy=\left[\frac{y^2}{2}+2y-\frac{y^3}{3}\right]_{-1}^{2}=\left(2+4-\frac{8}{3}\right)-\left(\frac{1}{2}-2+\frac{1}{3}\right)=\frac{9}{2}$.

questions.q: Find the total area between $y=\sin x$ and $y=\cos x$ on $[0,\pi]$, accounting for the curves crossing at $x=\frac{\pi}{4}$.
questions.answer: On $[0,\frac{\pi}{4}]$, $\cos x\geq\sin x$; on $[\frac{\pi}{4},\pi]$, $\sin x\geq\cos x$. Total area $=\int_0^{\pi/4}(\cos x-\sin x)\,dx+\int_{\pi/4}^{\pi}(\sin x-\cos x)\,dx$. First: $[\sin x+\cos x]_0^{\pi/4}=\sqrt{2}-1$. Second: $[-\cos x-\sin x]_{\pi/4}^{\pi}=(1-0)-(-\sqrt{2})=1+\sqrt{2}$. Total $=(\sqrt{2}-1)+(1+\sqrt{2})=2\sqrt{2}\approx2.83$.
questions.explanation: On $[0,\frac{\pi}{4}]$, $\cos x\geq\sin x$; on $[\frac{\pi}{4},\pi]$, $\sin x\geq\cos x$. Total area $=\int_0^{\pi/4}(\cos x-\sin x)\,dx+\int_{\pi/4}^{\pi}(\sin x-\cos x)\,dx$. First: $[\sin x+\cos x]_0^{\pi/4}=\sqrt{2}-1$. Second: $[-\cos x-\sin x]_{\pi/4}^{\pi}=(1-0)-(-\sqrt{2})=1+\sqrt{2}$. Total $=(\sqrt{2}-1)+(1+\sqrt{2})=2\sqrt{2}\approx2.83$.

questions.q: Find the area enclosed by $y^2=4-x$ and $x=0$, choosing the more convenient variable of integration.
questions.target: Area using the more efficient variable of integration
questions.answer: Solving for $x$: $x=4-y^2$, bounded by $x=0$ (i.e. $y=\pm2$). Integrating with respect to $y$ is easier: Area $=\int_{-2}^{2}(4-y^2)\,dy=\left[4y-\frac{y^3}{3}\right]_{-2}^{2}=\left(8-\frac{8}{3}\right)-\left(-8+\frac{8}{3}\right)=\frac{16}{3}+\frac{16}{3}=\frac{32}{3}$.
questions.explanation: Solving for $x$: $x=4-y^2$, bounded by $x=0$ (i.e. $y=\pm2$). Integrating with respect to $y$ is easier: Area $=\int_{-2}^{2}(4-y^2)\,dy=\left[4y-\frac{y^3}{3}\right]_{-2}^{2}=\left(8-\frac{8}{3}\right)-\left(-8+\frac{8}{3}\right)=\frac{16}{3}+\frac{16}{3}=\frac{32}{3}$.

questions.q: Set up (but do not evaluate) the integral expression for the area of the region enclosed by $y=e^x$, $y=\ln x$, and the lines $x=1$ and $x=2$.
questions.answer: On $[1,2]$, $e^x\geq\ln x$ (since $e^x$ grows much faster). Area $=\int_1^2\left(e^x-\ln x\right)dx$.
questions.explanation: On $[1,2]$, $e^x\geq\ln x$ (since $e^x$ grows much faster). Area $=\int_1^2\left(e^x-\ln x\right)dx$.

questions.q: Find the area of the region bounded by $y=x^3-x$ and $y=0$ on $[-1,1]$, accounting for the sign change at $x=0$.
questions.answer: On $[-1,0]$, $x^3-x\geq0$; on $[0,1]$, $x^3-x\leq0$. Area $=\int_{-1}^0(x^3-x)\,dx+\left|\int_0^1(x^3-x)\,dx\right|$. $\int_{-1}^0(x^3-x)\,dx=\left[\frac{x^4}{4}-\frac{x^2}{2}\right]_{-1}^0=0-\left(\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{2}\right)=\frac{1}{4}$. By symmetry the second piece is also $\frac{1}{4}$. Total area $=\frac{1}{2}$.
questions.explanation: On $[-1,0]$, $x^3-x\geq0$; on $[0,1]$, $x^3-x\leq0$. Area $=\int_{-1}^0(x^3-x)\,dx+\left|\int_0^1(x^3-x)\,dx\right|$. $\int_{-1}^0(x^3-x)\,dx=\left[\frac{x^4}{4}-\frac{x^2}{2}\right]_{-1}^0=0-\left(\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{2}\right)=\frac{1}{4}$. By symmetry the second piece is also $\frac{1}{4}$. Total area $=\frac{1}{2}$.

questions.q: Two competing companies' profit rates (in thousands of dollars per year) are $P_1(t)=50-2t$ and $P_2(t)=30+t$ over the first 10 years. Find the total difference in cumulative profit between the two companies over this period, using the area between the curves.
questions.answer: Intersection: $50-2t=30+t \Rightarrow 20=3t \Rightarrow t=\frac{20}{3}\approx6.67$. For $t<\frac{20}{3}$, $P_1>P_2$; for $t>\frac{20}{3}$, $P_2>P_1$. Total absolute difference $=\left|\int_0^{20/3}(P_1-P_2)\,dt\right|+\left|\int_{20/3}^{10}(P_2-P_1)\,dt\right|$, which can be computed piecewise using $P_1-P_2=20-3t$.
questions.explanation: Intersection: $50-2t=30+t \Rightarrow 20=3t \Rightarrow t=\frac{20}{3}\approx6.67$. For $t<\frac{20}{3}$, $P_1>P_2$; for $t>\frac{20}{3}$, $P_2>P_1$. Total absolute difference $=\left|\int_0^{20/3}(P_1-P_2)\,dt\right|+\left|\int_{20/3}^{10}(P_2-P_1)\,dt\right|$, which can be computed piecewise using $P_1-P_2=20-3t$.

Find the total area between $y=x^3-36x$ and the $x$-axis on $[-6,6]$, accounting for the sign change at $x=-6,0,6$.
questions.answer: Final Answer: $648$. By symmetry, total area $=2\int_0^{6}\left(6^2x-x^3\right)dx=2\left[\frac{6^2x^2}{2}-\frac{x^4}{4}\right]_0^{6}=2\left(\frac{1296}{2}-\frac{1296}{4}\right)=2\left(\frac{1296}{4}\right)=\frac{1296}{2}=648$.

questions.q: Find the total area between $y=x^3-9x$ and the $x$-axis on $[-3,3]$, accounting for the sign change at $x=-3,0,3$.
questions.target: Area using the more efficient variable of integration
questions.answer: Final Answer: $\frac{81}{2}$. By symmetry, total area $=2\int_0^{3}\left(3^2x-x^3\right)dx=2\left[\frac{3^2x^2}{2}-\frac{x^4}{4}\right]_0^{3}=2\left(\frac{81}{2}-\frac{81}{4}\right)=2\left(\frac{81}{4}\right)=\frac{81}{2}=\frac{81}{2}$.

What is the area of the region enclosed by $y = x^2$ and $y = 4$?
questions.target: Area Between Curves Integrated with Respect to x
questions.answer: Intersection points: $x^2 = 4 \Rightarrow x = \pm 2$. Area $= \int_{-2}^2 (4 - x^2) dx = 2[4x - \frac{x^3}{3}]_0^2 = 2(8 - \frac{8}{3}) = 2(\frac{16}{3}) = \frac{32}{3}$.
questions.explanation: Intersection points: $x^2 = 4 \Rightarrow x = \pm 2$. Area $= \int_{-2}^2 (4 - x^2) dx = 2[4x - \frac{x^3}{3}]_0^2 = 2(8 - \frac{8}{3}) = 2(\frac{16}{3}) = \frac{32}{3}$.

questions.q: Which integral represents the area enclosed by $y = \sin x$ and $y = \cos x$ from $x = 0$ to $x = \frac{\pi}{4}$?
questions.target: Area Between Curves Integrated with Respect to x
questions.answer: On $[0, \pi/4]$, $\cos x \geq \sin x$. The upper curve is $\cos x$ and lower is $\sin x$, so $\int_0^{\pi/4} (\cos x - \sin x) dx$.
questions.explanation: On $[0, \pi/4]$, $\cos x \geq \sin x$. The upper curve is $\cos x$ and lower is $\sin x$, so $\int_0^{\pi/4} (\cos x - \sin x) dx$.

questions.q: When is it advantageous to integrate with respect to $y$ rather than $x$?
questions.target: Area Between Curves Integrated with Respect to y
choices: When the boundary curves are expressed as $x = f(y)$ and solving for $y$ requires multiple piecewise branches
questions.answer: Integrating with respect to $y$ (right curve minus left curve) simplifies the setup whenever solving for $y$ yields plus/minus roots and splits the region into multiple integrals.
questions.explanation: Integrating with respect to $y$ (right curve minus left curve) simplifies the setup whenever solving for $y$ yields plus/minus roots and splits the region into multiple integrals.

questions.q: The graphs of $y = x^3$ and $y = x$ enclose how many symmetric regions?
questions.answer: Intersections: $x^3 - x = 0 \Rightarrow x(x - 1)(x + 1) = 0 \Rightarrow x = -1, 0, 1$. The curves enclose $2$ symmetric regions (on $[-1, 0]$ and $[0, 1]$).
questions.explanation: Intersections: $x^3 - x = 0 \Rightarrow x(x - 1)(x + 1) = 0 \Rightarrow x = -1, 0, 1$. The curves enclose $2$ symmetric regions (on $[-1, 0]$ and $[0, 1]$).

questions.q: Why does $\int_{-1}^1 (x - x^3) dx = 0$ NOT represent the enclosed area?
choices: The integrand is odd, causing positive and negative signed areas to cancel out
The curves do not intersect at $0$
questions.answer: A definite integral computes net signed area. For true area, one must integrate $|f(x) - g(x)|$.
questions.explanation: A definite integral computes net signed area. For true area, one must integrate $|f(x) - g(x)|$.

questions.q: Find the area enclosed by $y = e^x, y = e^{-x},$ and the vertical line $x = 1$.
questions.answer: Intersections: $e^x = e^{-x} \Rightarrow x = 0$. On $[0, 1]$, $e^x \geq e^{-x}$. Area $= \int_0^1 (e^x - e^{-x}) dx = [e^x + e^{-x}]_0^1 = (e + e^{-1}) - (1 + 1) = e + \frac{1}{e} - 2$.
questions.explanation: Intersections: $e^x = e^{-x} \Rightarrow x = 0$. On $[0, 1]$, $e^x \geq e^{-x}$. Area $= \int_0^1 (e^x - e^{-x}) dx = [e^x + e^{-x}]_0^1 = (e + e^{-1}) - (1 + 1) = e + \frac{1}{e} - 2$.
